chunks.title: JavaScript Promises
chunks.text: The promise object represents the eventual completion or failure of an asynchronous operation

chunks.title: JavaScript Promises
chunks.text: and its resulting value.

chunks.title: JavaScript Promises
chunks.text: It's like a placeholder for a value that you are waiting on.

chunks.title: JavaScript Promises
chunks.text: A promise can be in one of three states, pending, fulfilled, or rejected.

chunks.title: JavaScript Promises
chunks.text: When the promise is pending, JavaScript continues code execution.

chunks.title: JavaScript Promises
chunks.text: This way, the promise, or value that you are waiting on, does not cause your program

chunks.title: JavaScript Promises
chunks.text: to freeze.

chunks.title: JavaScript Promises
chunks.text: Eventually, the promise is either fulfilled or rejected and JavaScript goes back to that

chunks.title: JavaScript Promises
chunks.text: code block to execute the appropriate operation.

chunks.title: JavaScript Promises
chunks.text: Here is the basic layout of a promise.

chunks.title: JavaScript Promises
chunks.text: We create a variable and assign it to a new promise.

chunks.title: JavaScript Promises
chunks.text: The promise accepts a function with two parameters, resolve and reject.

chunks.title: JavaScript Promises
chunks.text: Within this function, we execute our asynchronous operation.

chunks.title: JavaScript Promises
chunks.text: Some examples of this would be getting data from another source, or downloading a file,

chunks.title: JavaScript Promises
chunks.text: or any other operation that will take an undetermined amount of time.

chunks.title: JavaScript Promises
chunks.text: After that, we determine whether we should resolve or reject the promise dependent on

chunks.title: JavaScript Promises
chunks.text: the success or failure of our asynchronous operation.

chunks.title: JavaScript Promises
chunks.text: Now that the promise is constructed, we can execute it.

chunks.title: JavaScript Promises
chunks.text: We call the promise to initiate it.

chunks.title: JavaScript Promises
chunks.text: We use .then to look for the promise to enter the fulfilled state.

chunks.title: JavaScript Promises
chunks.text: .then accepts a function that receives the resolved value from the resolve method.

chunks.title: JavaScript Promises
chunks.text: We can then do something with the results.

chunks.title: JavaScript Promises
chunks.text: After that, we can use .catch to look for the promise to enter the rejected state.

chunks.title: JavaScript Promises
chunks.text: .catch also accepts a function that receives any errors from our reject method.

text: The promise object represents the eventual completion or failure of an asynchronous operation and its resulting value. It's like a placeholder for a value that you are waiting on. A promise can be in one of three states, pending, fulfilled, or rejected. When the promise is pending, JavaScript continues code execution. This way, the promise, or value that you are waiting on, does not cause your program to freeze. Eventually, the promise is either fulfilled or rejected and JavaScript goes back to that code block to execute the appropriate operation. Here is the basic layout of a promise. We create a variable and assign it to a new promise. The promise accepts a function with two parameters, resolve and reject. Within this function, we execute our asynchronous operation. Some examples of this would be getting data from another source, or downloading a file, or any other operation that will take an undetermined amount of time. After that, we determine whether we should resolve or reject the promise dependent on the success or failure of our asynchronous operation. Now that the promise is constructed, we can execute it. We call the promise to initiate it. We use .then to look for the promise to enter the fulfilled state. .then accepts a function that receives the resolved value from the resolve method. We can then do something with the results. After that, we can use .catch to look for the promise to enter the rejected state. .catch also accepts a function that receives any errors from our reject method. This has been a 90 second JavaScript January.
